episodes.request: The release notes in the digest are not in the same order as in feeds/releases.rss. Is that a bug? Please just look, don't change anything.

steps.thought: Read the README first to see what order the digest promises.
steps.output:
# feedsync

A small command-line tool that turns the team's feeds into one Markdown digest.

## Usage

    node --experimental-strip-types bin/feedsync.ts digest
    node --experimental-strip-types bin/feedsync.ts digest --config feeds.json --limit 3
    npm run digest

feedsync reads the feed list in `feeds.json`:

    {"feeds": [{"name": "Engineering blog", "source": "feeds/blog.rss"}, ...]}

A source is a file path relative to the directory of `feeds.json`, or an `https://` URL.
The files in `feeds/` are snapshots of the live feeds for working offline. Only RSS 2.0
feeds are supported for now.

The digest has one section per feed, in the order of `feeds.json`, with the newest items
first: at most `--limit` items per feed (5 by default), each as
`- YYYY-MM-DD [title](link)` with the date in UTC. Items without a date come last. A feed
that cannot be read stops the digest with a message, and the command exits with status 2.

## Development

    npm test

There are no dependencies: the code is TypeScript run directly by Node 22 with
`--experimental-strip-types`, and the tests use `node:test`.

steps.thought: The ordering is done in digest.ts; read it.

finish.thought: The order difference is the documented newest-first sorting, not a bug.
finish.report: It is not a bug. renderDigest in src/digest.ts sorts each feed's items with newestFirst before it applies the limit, so the digest lists the newest items first whatever order the feed file uses; items without a date keep their order and come last. The README documents this. feeds/releases.rss happens to list its items newest first already (gateway 4.2.0 on 30 October, billing-api 2.7.1 on 26 October, gateway 4.1.3 on 19 October, cli 1.9.0 on 12 October), so its section in the digest matches the file. The engineering blog snapshot is the one whose items are not in date order in the file.

episodes.request: Could feedsync read the engineering blog straight from its URL instead of the snapshot in feeds/? What happens when the URL cannot be reached?

steps.thought: Check how the command line turns read errors into output.
See how the feed list is configured today.

finish.thought: URL sources are supported already, with a timeout and an error path.
finish.report: Yes, without any code change: readSource in src/sources.ts treats a source that starts with http:// or https:// as a URL and fetches it with a 10 second timeout (FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS); any other source is a file path relative to the directory of feeds.json. feeds.json lists the two snapshots, feeds/blog.rss and feeds/releases.rss, so switching the blog to its URL is a one-line change there. If the URL cannot be reached, or answers with an HTTP error, readSource throws a SourceError (`could not fetch <url>: ...`), and main in src/cli.ts prints `feedsync: ` followed by that message and exits with status 2 without printing a digest. One unreachable feed therefore stops the whole digest.
